text.en: Meena saw a methane flame in the school lab. "Carbon compounds burn well," said her teacher.

Many simple organic compounds have covalent bonds. Their melting points and other properties depend on their structures and interactions. They are classified by the carbon chain as open-chain or acyclic and closed-chain or cyclic compounds. Hydrocarbons are compounds of carbon and hydrogen only, and they are saturated alkanes or unsaturated alkenes and alkynes.
A carbon-carbon double or triple bond makes a chain unsaturated. A structural formula shows whether such bonds are present. Members of a homologous series share a functional-group pattern and general formula, and neighbouring members differ by CH₂. Members have similar chemical properties and gradually changing physical properties.
IUPAC nomenclature gives every organic compound a systematic name, with a root word for the number of carbons, a prefix and a suffix for the functional group. The rules for naming include choosing the longest chain, numbering it and naming the substituents.
Carbon forms many compounds by sharing electrons in covalent bonds. Their melting points and other properties vary with molecular structure.

text.en: A double or triple carbon-carbon bond makes the chain unsaturated. You can identify unsaturation by reading the bond lines in a structural formula.

text.en: A homologous series is a family with a shared functional-group pattern and a general formula. Adjacent members differ in composition by one C H two unit.

board.text: hydrocarbon

text.en: Carbon has four outer-shell electrons. In many common compounds, it shares electron pairs so each carbon forms a total of four bonds when bond order is counted.

board.text: Carbon usually makes four covalent bonds

text.en: One line is a single bond. Two lines mean a double bond, and three lines mean a triple bond.

board.text: A bond line represents a shared electron pair

text.en: Carbon can make stable carbon-carbon bonds, building chains and rings. This ability is called catenation.

board.text: Carbon atoms can join one another

text.en: A carbon skeleton can follow one path or split into branches. The formula alone may not reveal how it is connected.

board.text: Open chains can be straight or branched

text.en: In a cyclic compound, some atoms are connected around a ring. Open-chain and cyclic describe structure.

board.text: Cyclic compounds contain a closed loop

text.en: Methane and ethane are hydrocarbons. Ethanol also contains oxygen, so it is an organic compound but not a hydrocarbon.

board.text: Hydrocarbons contain carbon and hydrogen only

text.en: After each carbon uses one bond to join the other carbon, each can bond to three hydrogen atoms. The formula is C two H six.

board.text: Ethane has a carbon-carbon single bond

text.en: Two bonds connect the carbon atoms. Each has space for two hydrogen atoms, giving C two H four.

board.text: Ethene has a carbon-carbon double bond

text.en: Three bonds connect the carbon atoms. Each carbon has one bond left for hydrogen, giving C two H two.

board.text: Ethyne has a carbon-carbon triple bond

text.en: An open-chain alkane has single carbon-carbon bonds only. A double or triple bond makes the chain unsaturated.

board.text: Saturation depends on the carbon bonds

text.en: In ethene, each carbon has a double bond to the other carbon and two single bonds to hydrogen. The total bond order at each carbon is four.

board.text: Bond count helps check a drawing

text.en: A functional group is a structural feature associated with characteristic reactions. An alcohol contains a hydroxyl group attached to a suitable carbon atom.

board.text: A functional group helps identify a family

text.en: The group written C O O H is called the carboxyl group. Ethanoic acid contains this group.

board.text: Identify the carboxyl group

text.en: Both contain a carbonyl group. In an aldehyde it is at the end of the carbon chain. In a ketone it is within the chain.

board.text: A ketone and an aldehyde differ in position

text.en: Methane, ethane and propane are successive members of the alkane series. Each neighbour has one more carbon and two more hydrogens.

board.text: A homologous series extends the carbon chain

text.en: Within one family, larger molecules often have higher boiling points. Similar chemical properties do not make all physical properties identical.

board.text: Physical properties can change gradually

text.en: Meth means one carbon, eth means two, prop means three, and but means four in the parent chain.

board.text: Name roots indicate chain length

text.en: Ethane has a single connection between the two carbons. Ethene has a double bond, and ethyne has a triple bond.

board.text: Use the ending to read important bonds

text.en: A name can include a number showing where a group or multiple bond begins. For but-two-ene the double bond starts at carbon two.

board.text: Numbers can locate a feature

text.en: Both names start with eth because each has two carbons. Ethanol belongs to the alcohol family and ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid.

board.text: Ethanol and ethanoic acid differ in their groups

text.en: A soap molecule has a part that mixes well with water and a long part that associates with oils. The two ends help loosen grease.

board.text: A cleaning molecule has two kinds of ends

text.en: The oil-friendly tails can gather around a grease droplet while the water-friendly heads face outward. The droplets can then be carried away in water.

board.text: Soap can package oily dirt in clusters

problem.en: Which formula belongs to the two-carbon hydrocarbon with a double bond?

text.en: Join the carbons with two lines.

why.en: The double bond uses two of each carbon’s four bonds.

text.en: Add two hydrogens to each carbon. The formula is C₂H₄ and its name is ethene.

why.en: Two remaining single bonds per carbon attach to hydrogen.

problem.en: Methane is CH₄ and ethane is C₂H₆. What differs between these neighbours?

text.en: Subtract the atom counts in CH₄ from the counts in C₂H₆.

why.en: Ethane has one extra carbon and two extra hydrogens.

text.en: The composition changes by CH₂.

why.en: That is the step between neighbouring members of the alkane series.

problem.en: Why are ethanol and ethanoic acid in different families despite having two carbons?

text.en: Ethanol has an alcohol group and ethanoic acid has a carboxyl group.

why.en: A name’s chain-length root does not tell you every feature.

text.en: The different groups give the compounds different chemical behaviour.
